plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers that attract bees and butterflies. Widely grown in gardens and commercial fields for essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large flower head made of hundreds of tiny florets surrounded by yellow ray petals. Fields of sunflowers are at their peak in late July.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated in Ukraine, Russia, France, Spain, and the central United States
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds track the sun from east to west during the day, a behavior called heliotropism, but mature blooms stay facing east.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with daisy-like pink-purple petals drooping around a spiky orange-brown central cone. It is a favorite of pollinators and goldfinches.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in prairies and open woodlands, and widely grown in gardens
plants.funFact: Native Americans used Echinacea medicinally for centuries, and it remains one of the best-selling herbal supplements today.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: An upright evergreen shrub of southeastern Australia that produces spectacular crimson flower heads up to 15 cm across, surrounded by showy red bracts. It blooms at the end of the Australian winter and into spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (begins around August, with early blooms possible in late July)
plants.location: Sandstone ridges and forests of New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales, and its name comes from the Eora Aboriginal word meaning 'seen from afar'.
